name: Ishmael
description: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: This is before chapter 21, while the child was still in her womb: thou shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael, because the Lord hath heard thy affliction. Ishmael means affliction heard, and his name is important to future prophecy.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Abram was fourscore and six years old, eighty six, when Hagar bare Ishmael. Ishmael was Abram's firstborn, but the covenant did not go to Ishmael; the covenant goes through the twelve tribes of Israel.

Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

points: The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

points: These are the generations of Ishmael: Nebajoth the firstborn, and Kedar (that is Kedar, the Saudi Arabians today), Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael, by their towns and by their castles: twelve princes according to their nations. Pay attention to that: Ishmael had twelve princes, and each had a nation. I am about to show you something concerning the Sunni and the Shia.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Read from the screen: Sunni Muslims generally do not believe in the specific doctrine of the twelfth imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi, as defined by Shia Islam. Al-Mahdi means the guided one. Sunni tradition acknowledges a future Mahdi who will appear before the end times, but does not believe he is a hidden imam, the son of the eleventh imam, currently in occultation. The belief that there are twelve specific divinely appointed imams, culminating in a currently living hidden imam, is a core pillar of Twelver Shia Islam. Remember how many princes Ishmael had: twelve. The Twelver Shia literally believe there are twelve leaders that came from Muhammad, twelve successors, and that the twelfth imam disappeared in the ninth century and is going to return in these last days. Many Sunni scholars accept hadiths, their writings of prophecy and the sayings of Muhammad, that the Mahdi will come, but they believe he will be born in the future. So both the Sunni and the Shia are expecting a Mahdi, an anointed one, a guided one, who they say returns before Christ returns. That is their form of a Christ returning; not Christ, but some anointed one. I know some of you have never heard the Nation of Islam talk about a Mahdi.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: The generations of Ishmael list twelve princes according to their nations, exactly as the Most High promised in Genesis 17:20. Ishmael lived an hundred and thirty and seven years and died in the presence of all his brethren.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

points: The sons of Abraham are named, Isaac and Ishmael, and then the twelve sons of Ishmael are set down in order.
The generations of Ishmael are listed before the record returns to the promised seed through Isaac.
